| `node_ids` | array | yes | Array of source NodeGuid strings (from get_graph_nodes) to copy. |
| `dst_anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Destination UAnimBlueprint path/name. |
| `src_graph` | string | no | Source graph name (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `dst_graph` | string | no | Destination graph name (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `offset_x` | number | no | X offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |
| `offset_y` | number | no | Y offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ copied_count, id_map:{old->new}, imported_nodes[], missing_node_ids[], saved }`

## `create_anim_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Create an Animation Blueprint (parent UAnimInstance) for a skeleton at package_path/name with the editor factory, compile it and save it; an existing Animation Blueprint at that path is returned unchanged (already_existed=true). Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. Returns asset_path, generated_class and target_skeleton_set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new Animation Blueprint |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Optional skeleton path; defaults to /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, skeleton_path: string, generated_class: string, is_anim_instance: bool, target_skeleton_set: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_anim_composite`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UAnimComposite asset bound to a USkeleton, under /Game. Idempotent: a UAnimComposite already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'AnimComp_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, composite_path, skeleton, num_segments, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_anim_montage`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save an empty-but-valid UAnimMontage asset under /Game. Idempotent: a UAnimMontage already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'AM_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Montage slot name (e.g. DefaultSlot) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, montage_path, skeleton_path, slot_names, slot_name, slot_count, section_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_anim_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UAnimSequence at package_path/anim_name bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton) and save it; its data model gets frame_rate rounded to whole fps and round(length_seconds * fps) frames, but no bone tracks or curves. Idempotent: a UAnimSequence already at that path is returned unchanged (already_existed=true, saved=false, length and rate not applied) and nothing is saved; another asset class there or an unknown skeleton is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and the new asset stays in memory only. Fill it with set_anim_bone_track_keys (identity keys when keys is omitted) or add_anim_float_curve; inspect it with get_anim_sequence_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_name` | string | yes | Asset name (no path). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |
| `length_seconds` | number | no | Sequence length in seconds (default 1.0) |
| `frame_rate` | number | no | Sampling frame rate in fps (default 30) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, anim_name, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, success, saved, save_error, already_existed, message }`

## `create_blend_space`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a blend space asset under /Game -- a 2D UBlendSpace (default), a UBlendSpace1D, or an aim offset (UAimOffsetBlendSpace or UAimOffsetBlendSpace1D) picked by blend_space_type -- and write every axis setting it is given (name, range and grid divisions of the X axis, and of the Y axis on a 2D type) before rebuilding its runtime data. Idempotent: a blend space already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved (blend_space_type then reports the class it already has). An unknown blend_space_type, one that contradicts is_1d, an axis minimum not below its maximum, a grid below 1 or a Y-axis param on a 1D type is refused before anything is created. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'BS_Example'). |
| `asset_name` | string | no | Alias of name. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `blend_space_type` | string | no | Optional class to create: BlendSpace (2D, default) \| BlendSpace1D \| AimOffset (2D UAimOffsetBlendSpace) \| AimOffset1D (UAimOffsetBlendSpace1D), any case. Omitted, is_1d picks BlendSpace1D or BlendSpace. |
| `is_1d` | boolean | no | If true create a 1D BlendSpace, else 2D (default false); when blend_space_type is also given they must agree. |
| `axis_name` | string | no | X-axis display name (default 'Speed'; 'Yaw' for an aim offset) |
| `axis_min` | number | no | X-axis minimum value (default 0; -90 for an aim offset); must be below axis_max. |
| `min_value` | number | no | Alias of axis_min. |
| `axis_max` | number | no | X-axis maximum value (default 100; 90 for an aim offset) |
| `max_value` | number | no | Alias of axis_max. |
| `axis_grid` | number | no | Optional X-axis grid divisions, an integer >= 1 (default: the engine's 4). |
| `num_grid_points` | number | no | Alias of axis_grid. |
| `y_axis_name` | string | no | Optional Y-axis display name, 2D types only (default 'Pitch' for an aim offset; otherwise the engine's 'None' is kept). |
| `y_axis_min` | number | no | Optional Y-axis minimum, 2D types only (default 0; -90 for an aim offset); must be below y_axis_max. |
| `y_axis_max` | number | no | Optional Y-axis maximum, 2D types only (default 100; 90 for an aim offset). |
| `y_axis_grid` | number | no | Optional Y-axis grid divisions, 2D types only, an integer >= 1 (default: the engine's 4). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton) |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, blend_space_path, blend_space_type, is_1d, skeleton_path, axis_name, axis_min, axis_max, axis_grid_num, y_axis_name?, y_axis_min?, y_axis_max?, y_axis_grid_num?, sample_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_control_rig_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a Control Rig Blueprint (non-modular) at package_path/name with UControlRigBlueprintFactory, compile it and save it. Idempotent: an existing Control Rig Blueprint there is returned unchanged (already_existed=true). Returns asset_path, generated_class, is_control_rig and saved; refused while PIE runs unless force is set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder starting with "/", e.g. "/Game/Rigs"; a trailing slash is ignored |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Control Rig Blueprint, e.g. "CR_Hero" |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, generated_class: string, is_control_rig: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `create_editable_skeleton`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a USkeleton at package_path/name by duplicating an existing skeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton), then save it, so add_bone, set_bone_transform, add_virtual_bone and the other bone tools edit a project copy instead of engine content. Idempotent by path: a skeleton already there is returned untouched with created=false and saved=false. A package_path that does not start with a slash, a source that does not exist or is not a skeleton, or another kind of asset at the target is an error, and nothing is created. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error and keeps the new skeleton in memory. A mesh to go with it: duplicate_asset on a skeletal mesh (destination_path); inspect the result: get_skeleton_info (load_full_data=true).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder starting with a slash, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new skeleton, e.g. "SK_Creature_Skeleton"; with package_path it gives the asset path. |
| `source_skeleton` | string | no | Asset path of the skeleton to duplicate, e.g. "/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton", which is also the default. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source: string, bone_count: int, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_ik_retargeter`

*Additive.*

Create and save a UIKRetargeter asset wiring source + target IK Rigs. An existing retargeter at that path is rewired and saved when either rig differs; when it already uses both rigs nothing changes, nothing is saved (saved=false) and a note says so. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Retargeter |
| `source_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the source UIKRigDefinition (copy FROM) |
| `target_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the target UIKRigDefinition (copy TO) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source_ik_rig: string, target_ik_rig: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_ik_rig`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UIKRigDefinition asset and set its source skeletal mesh.  Idempotent: an existing rig is loaded and only given the mesh, then saved, when it has another one; when it already has that mesh, or the mesh does not load or the engine refuses it (skeletal_mesh_set false), nothing changes, nothing is saved and a note says why. The default skeletal_mesh_path is /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Rig |
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | no | Optional USkeletalMesh asset path; defaults to /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, skeletal_mesh: string, skeletal_mesh_set: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_pose_asset`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty UPoseAsset (no poses) at package_path/name, bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton), and save it; no undo transaction. Idempotent: a UPoseAsset already at that path is returned untouched with already_existed=true and saved=false, even when bound to another skeleton, and nothing is saved. A name taken by another asset class or an unknown skeleton is an error, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Add poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset; to build one from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'Pose_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, pose_asset_path, skeleton, num_poses, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UPoseAsset built from a real UAnimSequence's frames and save it. Idempotent: a UPoseAsset already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_name` | string | yes | Name for the new UPoseAsset. |
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the source UAnimSequence. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, pose_asset_name, source_anim, skeleton_path, num_poses, created, success, already_existed, saved, save_error }`

## `create_pose_search_database`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UPoseSearchDatabase data asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/MCP) whose Schema is the UPoseSearchSchema at schema_path, with no animation assets yet, then save it. Idempotent: a database already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed true and saved false, nothing saved, its schema_path read from it; the requested schema is not applied, and not even loaded. An invalid path, an asset of another class there, or for a new database a schema that does not load, is an error; a failed save of a new database makes success false. Create the schema with create_pose_search_schema; change the schema of an existing database with set_pose_search_database_schema; add animations with add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database, then run build_pose_search_database_index.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchDatabase_Example'). |
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of an existing UPoseSearchSchema (required); loaded only for a database this call creates. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path (default /Game/MCP). |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_pose_search_schema`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UPoseSearchSchema data asset at package_path/name (package_path defaults to /Game/MCP) bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path, with sample_rate clamped to 1..240 and the default Trajectory and Pose channels, then save it. Idempotent: a schema already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed true and saved false, nothing saved, its skeleton_path and skeleton_paths read from it; the requested skeleton and sample_rate are not applied, and that skeleton is not even loaded. An invalid path, an asset of another class there, or for a new schema a skeleton that does not load, is an error; a failed save of a new schema makes success false. Next create a database with create_pose_search_database; add channels with add_pose_search_channel_to_schema, change settings with set_pose_search_schema_properties, and inspect it with inspect_pose_search_schema.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'PoseSearchSchema_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path (default /Game/MCP); trailing slashes are stripped. |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the USkeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton); loaded only for a schema this call creates. |
| `sample_rate` | number | no | Schema SampleRate (int, ClampMin=1, ClampMax=240; default 30); out-of-range values are clamped, and it is applied only to a schema this call creates. |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, schema_path, skeleton_path, skeleton_paths, sample_rate, schema_cardinality, channel_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_retarget_pose`

*Additive.*

Create a new retarget pose for editing in an IK Retargeter through its controller, then save the asset.  The engine makes the name unique, so read pose_name back. The pose is set as the current pose after creation, ready for bone rotation edits via set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Retargeter asset. |
| `pose_name` | string | yes | Name for the new retarget pose |
| `source_or_target` | string | no | Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target" |

**Returns:** `{ ik_retargeter_path: string, pose_name: string, source_or_target: string, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a new morph target on a skeletal mesh asset in memory only, for the rest of the editor session: it is never saved (persisted_to_disk is always false), and a mesh rebuild or reload drops any morph the mesh's imported source data does not contain. Each LOD gets one tiny seed delta on vertex 0 so the morph counts as valid; write real deltas with set_morph_target_deltas. Marks the mesh dirty. Idempotent: an existing name returns created=false and already_exists=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/SKM_Example) |
| `morph_target_name` | string | yes | Name for the new morph target |

**Returns:** `{ morph_target_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, created: bool, persisted_to_disk: bool, total_morph_targets: int, note: string }`

## `disconnect_anim_graph_pins`

*Destructive.*

Break AnimGraph pin links: a specific source->target link, or ALL links on the source pin. Use the specific form to insert a node into an existing chain (break A->B, then wire A->N and N->B). Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `source_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the source node. |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Pin name on the source node. |
| `target_node_id` | string | no | NodeGuid of the target node (optional; if omitted, breaks ALL links on source_pin). |
| `target_pin` | string | no | Pin name on the target node (optional; required if target_node_id is given). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ disconnected, broke_all, source_node_id, source_pin, saved }`

## `disconnect_ik_goal_from_solver`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Disconnect a goal from a solver, removing that solver's per-goal effector/settings, through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  Inverse of connect_ik_goal_to_solver. Idempotent: disconnecting a goal that isn't connected is a success with was_connected:false, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved. An out-of-range solver_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, goal_name: string, solver_index: int, connected: bool, was_connected: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `edit_anim_notify`

*Destructive.*

Edit an existing FAnimNotifyEvent on a UAnimSequence (identified by name + occurrence) in an undo transaction and save it. No editable field is an error before anything changes; edits that leave the event as it is are a success with applied=false, applied_count 0 and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `notify_name` | string | yes | NotifyName of the event to edit (FName). Names are not unique; see occurrence_index. |
| `occurrence_index` | number | no | Zero-based index AMONG events sharing notify_name (default 0) |
| `time` | number | no | New trigger time in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetTime). Optional. |
| `duration` | number | no | New duration in seconds (FAnimNotifyEvent::SetDuration; meaningful for notify-state). Optional. |
| `trigger_chance` | number | no | New NotifyTriggerChance in [0,1]. Optional. |
| `trigger_weight_threshold` | number | no | New TriggerWeightThreshold. Optional. |
| `montage_tick_type` | string | no | New MontageTickType: 'Queued' or 'BranchingPoint'. Optional. |
| `track_index` | number | no | New TrackIndex (zero-based). Optional. |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, notify_name, occurrence_index, matched_count, notify, applied_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `edit_blend_space_sample`

*Destructive.*

Edit a blend sample (by index): blend value and/or animation. At least one of blend_value / animation_path is required; both are individually optional so you can retime a sample without touching its animation, or swap the animation without moving it. A sample that already has those values is a success with value_edited=false, animation_replaced=false and saved=false, and the blend space is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blendspace_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UBlendSpace. |
| `index` | number | yes | Index of the sample to edit. |
| `blend_value` | any | no | New blend position: single number (1D) or array of up to 3 numbers (optional). |
| `animation_path` | string | no | Full asset path to a UAnimSequence to replace the sample's animation (optional). |

**Returns:** `{ blendspace_path, index, value_edited, animation_replaced, num_samples, samples, saved, save_error, message }`

## `evaluate_pose_search_query`

*Read-only.*

Run a live motion-matching query on a PIE/Game actor against a loaded UPoseSearchDatabase (UPoseSearchLibrary::MotionMatch) and return the best-match asset + search cost, plus the query trajectory. Diagnoses why a chooser returns null. Best-effort: per-channel cost is not exposed by the BlueprintPure result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | UPoseSearchDatabase asset path to search (required). |
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) \| 'editor' forces the editor world. |
| `actor_name` | string | no | Actor name or label whose AnimInstance drives the query. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn. |
| `pose_history_name` | string | no | Tag of the PoseSearchHistoryCollector anim-graph node used to build the query (default 'PoseHistory'). |
| `max_trajectory_samples` | number | no | Cap on emitted query trajectory samples (&lt;=0 = all; default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ world_mode, actor_name, actor_resolved, anim_instance_class, pose_history_name, pose_history_found, database_path, query_trajectory_samples[], trajectory_sample_count, is_trajectory_empty, has_match, best_match_asset, best_match_database, best_cost, selected_time, is_continuing_pose_search, wanted_play_rate, is_mirrored, is_looping, per_channel_cost[], note, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }`

## `get_active_montages`

*Read-only.*

Report the AnimMontage(s) currently playing on a live PIE actor's skeletal mesh (useful for blend-out debugging).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor` | string | yes | Name, label, or full path of a live actor (resolved in the PIE world by default). |
| `component` | string | no | Optional skeletal mesh component name; defaults to the actor's primary USkeletalMeshComponent. |
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve the actor in: absent/'pie' (default, ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'editor' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ actor, actor_name, component, world, anim_instance_class, montage_count, is_any_montage_playing, top_montage_id, enumeration, montages: [{ index, montage_path, montage_name, is_top, current_section, position, normalized_position, length, play_rate, blend_weight, desired_weight, blend_time, is_playing, is_active, instance_id, slots:[string] }], world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `get_anim_asset_info`

*Read-only.*

Load any animation asset and report its class, skeleton and asset_type (montage, composite, pose, sequence, blendspace or animation_asset) plus the counts of that type: sections/slots/notifies, segments, poses/tracks/curves, length, samples. Read-only; get_montage_info, get_anim_sequence_info and get_blend_space_samples give detail.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the animation asset (UAnimMontage, UAnimComposite, UPoseAsset, UAnimSequence, or UBlendSpace) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, class, skeleton, num_segments, num_poses, section_count, slot_count, notify_count, sequence_length, rate_scale, num_tracks, num_curves, sample_count, asset_type }`

## `get_anim_blueprint_info`

*Read-only.*

Read an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: its Asset Registry identity (object path, class, package, is_loaded, and the size and timestamp of its .uasset, left out when no file is on disk), target skeleton and its bone count, parent and generated class, is_anim_instance, is_abstract, is_template, graph_count, and the state machines at the top level of every function graph (the AnimGraph included) with their graph and state counts (conduits not counted; machines nested inside states are not listed). anim_blueprint_path takes an object path, a package path or a short name searched under /Game; no match is an error, and so is a short name several anim blueprints share, with the candidates listed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Object path, package path or short name of the UAnimBlueprint asset |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, asset_class: string, package_name: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes: number?, file_size_kb: number?, file_size_mb: number?, last_modified: string?, target_skeleton: string, target_skeleton_set: bool, skeleton_bone_count: int, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, is_anim_instance: bool, is_abstract: bool, is_template: bool, graph_count: int, state_machine_count: int, state_machines: [{ name: string, graph_name: string, state_count: int }] }`

## `get_anim_curve_data`

*Read-only.*

Read one curve of a UAnimSequence without changing it: for a float curve its flags, num_keys and keys as time/value pairs; for a transform curve only flags and a summed num_keys. found=false (still a success) when the curve does not exist.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the curve to read |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, curve_type, found, num_keys, flags, time, value, keys }`

## `get_anim_graph_node_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read the internal FAnimNode struct of one AnimGraphNode, found by NodeGuid (node_id) in the AnimGraph or a nested graph_name, as typed JSON: the runtime settings (Pose History PoseCount/CollectorName, Slot SlotName, blend params), not the pin surface get_graph_nodes reports. Use it instead of get_properties, which cannot address a graph node by GUID; a non-anim node returns its EditAnywhere properties. Read-only; write with set_anim_graph_node_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target AnimGraphNode. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, node_class, node_struct, node_properties:{...} }`

## `get_anim_notifies`

*Read-only.*

List the notify events of a UAnimSequence without changing it: name, trigger time, duration, track_index and the notify_class or notify_state_class of each, plus num_notifies, and the names of its notify tracks in track order (track_names, track_count). Use get_montage_info for the notifies of a montage.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, num_notifies, notifies: [{ name, time, duration, track_index, notify_class?, notify_state_class? }], track_names: [string], track_count }`

## `get_anim_sequence_info`

*Read-only.*

Summarise one animation sequence (a UAnimSequence asset) from its data model: the skeleton it plays on, its length, frame rate and frame count, the names of its bone tracks, float curves and transform curves with their counts, how many sync markers it has, whether root motion is enabled, and its retarget source and reference-pose sequence. Read-only: it changes nothing and needs no PIE. A path that does not load as an AnimSequence is refused, a montage or blend space included -- get_anim_asset_info reads any animation asset. The keys of one curve come from get_anim_curve_data and the notify events from get_anim_notifies.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the sequence, e.g. "/Game/Anims/Run_Fwd" (package or object path). |
| `sequence_path` | string | no | Alias of anim_sequence_path; read only when anim_sequence_path is absent. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, num_bone_tracks, num_float_curves, transform_curve_count, bone_tracks: [string], float_curves: [string], transform_curves: [string], num_sync_markers, enable_root_motion, retarget_source, ref_pose_seq, success }`

## `get_anim_state_machine_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the nodes of one state machine of an Animation Blueprint without compiling or changing it: state_count counts the states, conduit_count the conduits and transition_count the transitions; states lists every state, conduit and alias node with its kind (class name) and graph position, transitions excluded. It also checks the machine by those counts: no states is an error, one an info, several without transitions a warning (is_valid is false only on an error); compile_anim_blueprint is the check that the machine compiles.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |
| `state_machine_name` | string | yes | Name of a state machine in the top-level AnimGraph, matched without case (get_anim_blueprint_info lists them). |

**Returns:** `{ state_machine, state_count, conduit_count, transition_count, states:[{name,kind,x,y}], is_valid, errors:[string], warnings:[string], info:[string] }`

## `get_blend_space_samples`

*Read-only.*

Read every sample of a UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D in index order (animation path, blend_x/blend_y/blend_z, rate_scale) plus num_samples and the per-axis input smoothing under interpolation. Read-only; change samples with add_blend_space_sample, edit_blend_space_sample or remove_blend_space_sample.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blendspace_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UBlendSpace. |

**Returns:** `{ animation, blend_x, blend_y, blend_z, rate_scale, blendspace_path, num_samples, samples }`

## `get_bone_transform`

*Read-only.*

Read the LOCAL reference-pose transform of a bone (parent-relative, not component space). Exact inverse of set_bone_transform: it reads the same raw ref-pose array that one writes, so a read-modify-write round trip is lossless.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Bone to read |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, found, location:[x,y,z], rotation:[p,y,r], scale:[x,y,z], bone_count, op: "get_bone_transform" }`

## `get_ik_bone_settings`

*Read-only.*

Get bone-specific settings for a bone within a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (rotation/position stiffness, axis limits Free/Limited/Locked, min/max angles, preferred angles); StretchLimb (the only other solver with per-bone settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: squashDirection vector). Only FullBodyIK and StretchLimb support per-bone settings; others return a `note`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to query settings for. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, bone_name: string, settings: object }`

## `get_ik_goal_settings`

*Read-only.*

Get goal-specific settings for a goal connected to a solver.  FullBodyIK returns snake_case keys (chain_depth, strength_alpha, pull_chain_alpha, pin_rotation); BodyMover (the only other solver with per-goal settings) is serialized generically (camelCase: influenceMultiplier, boneName). The goal must be connected to the solver first (connect_ik_goal_to_solver), else a `note` explains that. Solvers without per-goal settings return a `note`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal to query settings for. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, goal_name: string, settings: object }`

## `get_ik_retargeter_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the global structure of an IK Retargeter via its controller: source/target IK Rigs, the op-stack, per-op chain mappings, and the current poses.  Read-only. Chain mappings are per-op in 5.6+ (there is no global RootSettings on the UIKRetargeter in 5.8; detailed root/global settings live inside the ops themselves).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_ik_rig: string, target_ik_rig: string, op_count: int, ops: [{ op_index, op_name, enabled, parent_op, op_type }], chain_mappings: [{ op_name, target_chain, source_chain }], source: { current_pose, pelvis_bone, root_offset: {x,y,z} }, target: { current_pose, pelvis_bone, root_offset: {x,y,z} } }`

## `get_ik_rig_info`

*Read-only.*

Read an IK Rig asset: its skeletal mesh, the number of solvers, and every goal and retarget chain, or with chain_name just that retarget chain (start_bone, end_bone and the IK goal it drives) plus whether the rig has it. Read-only; a chain_name the rig does not have is not an error but found=false and an empty chains list. Solvers are counted, not listed: get_ik_solver_details reads one by index.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset (an IK Rig, not an IK Retargeter) |
| `chain_name` | string | no | Optional. Name of one retarget chain, matched without case: chains then lists only that chain and found says whether the rig has it. retarget_chain_count still counts every chain. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_count: int, goal_count: int, retarget_chain_count: int, skeletal_mesh: string, goals: [{ goal_name, bone_name }], chains: [{ chain_name, start_bone, end_bone, goal_name }], chain_name?: string, found?: bool }`

## `get_ik_solver_details`

*Read-only.*

Read one solver of an IK Rig asset by its 0-based stack index: solver_type (the solver struct name, e.g. "IKRigFullBodyIKSolver") and solver_type_canonical (FullBodyIK, Limb, ...), unique_name ("&lt;index+1> - &lt;display name>"), enabled, start and end bone (end_bone "None" for a solver type without one), the names of the goals connected to it, and its solver-specific settings -- FullBodyIK with the curated snake_case keys set_ik_solver_settings takes, every other solver type serialized generically from its live settings struct (camelCase property names). Read-only; an out-of-range solver_index or a rig that does not load is an error. get_ik_rig_info reads the goals and chains of the whole rig.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, solver_type: string, solver_type_canonical: string, unique_name: string, enabled: bool, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, connected_goal_count: int, connected_goals: [string], settings: object }`

## `get_montage_info`

*Read-only.*

Read a UAnimMontage without changing it: skeleton_path, section, slot and notify counts with their name lists, blend_in/blend_out times, blend modes, enable_auto_blend_out, blend_out_trigger_time, sync_group and sync_slot_index. Change them with set_montage_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, skeleton_path, section_count, slot_count, notify_count, sections, slots, notifies, blend_in, blend_out, blend_mode_in, blend_mode_out, enable_auto_blend_out, blend_out_trigger_time, sync_group, sync_slot_index }`

## `get_morph_target_deltas`

*Read-only.*

Read back the vertex deltas of a morph target on a specific LOD (inverse of set_morph_target_deltas).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `morph_target_name` | string | yes | Name of the morph target to read |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to read (default 0) |
| `max_deltas` | number | no | Optional cap on how many deltas to return (default 5000); the response is honestly marked truncated if the LOD has more |

**Returns:** `{ morph_target_name: string, lod_index: int, total_deltas: int, returned_deltas: int, truncated: bool, deltas: [{vertex_index, position_delta:{x,y,z}, normal_delta:{x,y,z}}] }`

## `get_pose_search_runtime_state`

*Read-only.*

Read-only report of the live motion-matching state on a PIE/Game actor (why a chooser returns null): its AnimInstance, its MotionTrajectory samples, whether a PoseSearchHistoryCollector node named pose_history_name exists, and (optionally) the target database's schema/channels.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `world` | string | no | Which world to resolve: absent (default) = prefer the live PIE/Game world, else the editor world \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what a server-driven character lives in) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'pie'/'game' force the live session (errors if none running) \| 'editor' forces the editor world. |
| `actor_name` | string | no | Actor name or label to inspect. Omitted = the first player controller's pawn (the locally-controlled character). |
| `pose_history_name` | string | no | Tag of the PoseSearchHistoryCollector anim-graph node to look up on the AnimInstance (default 'PoseHistory'). A missing node is the usual reason a query builds an empty pose portion. |
| `database_path` | string | no | Optional UPoseSearchDatabase asset path; when given, its schema_path/schema_cardinality/channels/animation_asset_count are included. |
| `max_trajectory_samples` | number | no | Cap on emitted trajectory samples (&lt;=0 = all; default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ world_mode, actor_name, actor_resolved, actor_resolved_by, skeletal_mesh_component, anim_instance_class, pose_history_name, pose_history_found, trajectory:{found,component,property,sample_count,is_trajectory_empty,samples[]}, is_trajectory_empty, database?:{database_path,schema_path,schema_cardinality,channel_count,channels[],animation_asset_count}, note, world_name, world_package, world_type, net_mode, pie_instance }`

## `get_retarget_poses`

*Read-only.*

List every retarget pose (source and target) of an IK Retargeter with its root translation delta and per-bone rotation deltas.  Read-only. Bone rotation deltas use the same quat keys as set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation (quat_x, quat_y, quat_z, quat_w).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |

*Read-only.*

Read one retarget op's live settings struct from an IK Retargeter by op index.  Read-only (no save). The settings keys are the op settings UPROPERTY names with only the first character lower-cased (FJsonObjectConverter convention), e.g. FK Chains op exposes lODThreshold, bEnabled, bDebugDraw, chainDrawSize, bDrawChainLines. op_type is the settings struct name (e.g. IKRetargetFKChainsOpSettings), which differs from get_ik_retargeter_info.ops[].op_type (the op struct name).

|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |
| `op_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the op in the retargeter's op stack. |

## `get_rig_control_value`

*Read-only.*

Read a Control Rig control's current value (typed per ERigControlType) and its limit min/max.  Round-trips set_rig_control_value / set_rig_control_limits.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, value: any, limit_enabled: bool, min: number?, max: number? }`

## `get_rig_hierarchy`

*Read-only.*

Read every element of a Control Rig Blueprint hierarchy in traversal order as elements [{name, type}], plus bone_count, null_count, control_count, curve_count, other_count (sockets, connectors and the rest) and total. Read-only: nothing is compiled or saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Control Rig Blueprint asset path, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Hero" |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, elements: [{name, type}] }`

## `get_rigvm_graph`

*Read-only.*

Read the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint, loaded by asset path: every node with its name, title, type (the rig-unit struct, or the node class otherwise) and top-level pins, each pin with its name, NodeName.PinName path, direction and is_execute, plus node_count and link_count. Links are only counted, not listed, and the sub-pins of struct pins are not expanded. Read-only: nothing is compiled or saved, and no PIE is needed. A path that is not a Control Rig Blueprint, or one with no default RigVM model, is an error. Use the pin paths with add_rigvm_link and set_rigvm_pin_default; add nodes with add_rigvm_node, take one out with remove_rigvm_node; the bones and controls of the rig: get_rig_hierarchy.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UControlRigBlueprint, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin". |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, nodes: [{ name: string, title: string, type: string, pin_count: int, pins: [{ name: string, path: string, direction: string, is_execute: bool }] }], node_count: int, link_count: int }`

## `get_skeletal_mesh_info`

*Read-only.*

Get detailed info about a skeletal mesh: LODs, materials, morph targets, sockets, bones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset (e.g. /Game/MyMesh) |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, num_lods: int, num_materials: int, num_morph_targets: int, num_sockets: int, num_bones: int, bone_names: [string], lod_info: [{lod_index, num_verts, num_sections}] }`

## `get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the settings of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path: screen size, material map entry count, CPU access, the build settings, the reduction settings and the flat LOD scalars (hysteresis, prioritization weight, morph error tolerance, skin cache usage, mesh deformer). Enums come back by name, e.g. "SMTC_NumOfTriangles" or "Auto", a form the setters accept. Nothing is written. A mesh that does not load, or a lod_index outside its LOD count, is an error. Each block has its setter: set_skeletal_mesh_lod_build_settings, set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings, and set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings (screen_size included). Per-LOD vertex counts: get_skeletal_mesh_info; triangle counts: get_asset_lod_settings; sections: get_skeletal_mesh_section_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `lod_index` | number | no | 0-based LOD index to read (default 0); it must be below the LOD count of the mesh |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, screen_size: float, num_material_map_entries: int, allow_cpu_access: bool, build_settings: {...}, reduction_settings: {...}, lod_hysteresis: float, weight_of_prioritization: float, morph_target_position_error_tolerance: float, skin_cache_usage: string, allow_mesh_deformer: bool }`

List the material slots of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, in slot-index order: slot name, assigned material and overlay material as object paths, "(none)" where a slot has none. Nothing is written; a mesh that does not load is an error. Pass a slot_index or slot_name from here to set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot to assign a material; get_skeletal_mesh_section_info gives the material_index each section of a LOD draws with; get_skeletal_mesh_info gives the slot count next to LODs, morph targets, sockets and bones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, num_material_slots: int, material_slots: [{slot_index, slot_name, material_path, overlay_material_path}] }`

## `get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets`

*Read-only.*

Get all morph targets on a skeletal mesh with delta counts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, count: int, morph_targets: [{name, has_valid_data, num_deltas_lod0}] }`

## `get_skeletal_mesh_section_info`

*Read-only.*

Get section data for a LOD: material index, triangle count, vertex count, flags.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to query (default 0) |

## `get_skeleton_info`

*Read-only.*

Find a Skeleton asset in the Asset Registry and report its object path, class path, package, whether it is loaded, the size and timestamp of its .uasset (left out when no file is on disk), and the skeletal meshes bound to it (mesh_count, mesh_paths, shared when more than one), all without loading it; nothing is changed. skeleton_name takes an object path, a package path or a short name searched under /Game; no match is an error, and so is a short name several skeletons share, with the candidates listed. Only with load_full_data true is the asset loaded, adding bone_count, the first 100 bones (name, index, parent_index) with bones_truncated, socket_count, slot_group_count and every virtual bone with its source and target. One bone's reference pose: get_bone_transform; a skeletal mesh: get_skeletal_mesh_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_name` | string | yes | Object path, package path, or bare short name of the Skeleton asset (resolved via mcp_common::ResolveAssetFlexible; an ambiguous short name errors out listing every candidate instead of picking one silently) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Alias of skeleton_name. |
| `load_full_data` | boolean | no | When true, loads the asset and reports bone list (capped at 100), sockets, slot groups and virtual bones (optional, default false) |

**Returns:** `{ skeleton_name: string, skeleton_path: string, skeleton_class: string, package_name: string, is_loaded: bool, file_size_bytes: number?, file_size_kb: number?, file_size_mb: number?, last_modified: string?, mesh_count: int, shared: bool, mesh_paths: [string], loaded_successfully: bool?, is_valid: bool?, bone_count: number?, bones: [{ name, index, parent_index }]?, bones_truncated: bool?, socket_count: number?, slot_group_count: number?, virtual_bone_count: number?, virtual_bone_names: [string]?, virtual_bones: [{ name, source_bone, target_bone }]?, load_error: string? }`

*Read-only.*

Read the full data-layer state of a UMotionWarpingComponent: the b_search_for_windows_in_anims_within_montages flag, every warp target (via GetWarpTargets(): its FName, static location/rotation, component path or null, bone name, b_follow_component, location/rotation offsets and location_offset_direction enum integer), the modifier count (via GetModifiers()), the runtime adapter class (GetOwnerAdapter()->GetClass()), and the protected switch-off-conditions array count (via reflection — FindFProperty&lt;FArrayProperty> + FScriptArrayHelper). | `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path or short name of the actor. |

*Read-only.*

Read-only walk of Schema, DatabaseAnimationAssets and Channels on a UPoseSearchDatabase

| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required). |

*Read-only.*

Read-only walk of a UPoseSearchSchema's public fields + FinalizedChannels. An empty finalized_channels / is_finalized:false is NOT a bug in this tool: the schema only gets finalized by AddDefaultChannels() or by a PostEditChange() on it, so a freshly authored schema reports none until something triggers that.

|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema (required). |

## `link_montage_sections`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Chain one montage section to the next by setting its NextSectionName.  add_montage_section creates sections but never links them; this writes FCompositeSection::NextSectionName so playback flows section -> next. Pass next_section_name "" or "None" to clear the link. Done in an undo transaction, then saved. Idempotent: the link the section already has is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing section whose link to set. |
| `next_section_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing section to play next (or "" / "None" to clear). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_name, next_section_name, linked, changed, section_count, sections, saved, save_error, message }`

## `move_ik_solver_in_stack`

*Destructive.*

Move the solver at from_index so that it ends up at to_index (both 0-based positions in the solver stack) of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset. An index outside the stack is an error and nothing moves; from_index equal to to_index is not an error but moved false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `from_index` | number | yes | Source 0-based solver index |
| `to_index` | number | yes | Target 0-based solver index, below the solver count |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, solver_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `play_animation`

*Destructive.*

Play an AnimMontage on a skeletal mesh component with UAnimInstance::Montage_Play at play_rate, then jump to start_section if playback started. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; the component needs an anim instance. playing/success mean Montage_Play returned a length above 0.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the AnimMontage (e.g. '/Game/Animations/MyMontage.MyMontage') |
| `play_rate` | number | no | Playback rate multiplier (optional, default 1.0) |
| `start_section` | string | no | Name of the section to jump to after play starts (optional) |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, montage_path: string, montage_name: string, playing: bool, play_rate: number, montage_length: number, return_value: number, success: bool, start_section: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `refresh_anim_montage_cache`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Re-run UAnimMontage::RefreshCacheData on a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction (it sorts the notifies, moves a notify off a missing or overlapping notify track, adding tracks as needed, and rebuilds the branching point markers) and save it. Idempotent: when the refresh rewrites none of those fields the reply is a success with refreshed=false and saved=false, the montage keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, refreshed, sequence_length, slot_count, section_count, saved, save_error, message }`

## `reimport_anim_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Reimport a UAnimSequence, or any reimportable asset (the class is not checked), from source_file_path or its first recorded source via FReimportManager, automated (no dialogs) and unsaved. A missing source is refused before the reimport, which would crash the editor on it, and a reimport the handler reports as failed is a failure too: both make success false with reimported=false, and the missing source a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `source_file_path` | string | no | Absolute path of the file to reimport from on disk (e.g. "D:/Art/Walk.fbx"); defaults to the first source file recorded in the asset import data. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, source_file_path, reimported, source_validated, note? }`
