## `remove_skeletal_mesh_morph_target`

*Destructive.*

Delete one morph target, by name, from a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, including its data in every LOD's source mesh, in one undo step, then save the mesh. Not idempotent: a name the mesh does not have is an error, so a repeat call fails instead of reporting it already gone. A mesh that does not load is an error, and so is a failed save (refused during PIE or under a read-only root, or a locked file), although the deletion stays in memory. remaining_morph_targets counts the morphs left. List names with get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets; rename with rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target; add one with create_skeletal_mesh_morph_target.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `morph_target_name` | string | yes | Name of the morph target to delete, as get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets lists it |

**Returns:** `{ morph_target_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, removed: bool, remaining_morph_targets: int }`

## `remove_skeletal_mesh_socket`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a socket from a skeletal mesh (and its skeleton twin). Idempotent: re-running with an absent socket returns already_removed=true without mutating the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to remove |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, removed: bool, already_removed: bool, socket_count: int }`

## `remove_skeleton_socket`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a socket from the socket list of a USkeleton asset and save it. Idempotent: a missing socket returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns socket_count and the remaining socket_names; sockets that exist only on a skeletal mesh are untouched (use remove_skeletal_mesh_socket).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to remove (case-insensitive). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, socket_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, socket_count: int, socket_names: [string], saved: bool }`

## `remove_virtual_bone`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a virtual bone from a USkeleton asset, named directly or found by its source and target bones, then save. Idempotent: no match returns removed false and already_absent true without saving. Returns the remaining virtual_bone_names; a failed save returns success false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `virtual_bone_name` | string | no | Full virtual bone name with its "VB " prefix, e.g. "VB pelvis_hand_r"; when given, source_bone and target_bone are ignored. |
| `source_bone` | string | no | Source bone name; used with target_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted. |
| `target_bone` | string | no | Target bone name; used with source_bone to resolve the virtual bone when virtual_bone_name is omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, virtual_bone_count: int, virtual_bone_names: [string], saved: bool }`

## `rename_anim_curve`

*Destructive.*

Rename a float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step) and save it; errors when the source curve does not exist or the rename is refused. The same name for both is a success with renamed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. Any curve_type other than transform means float. Returns renamed and saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `old_curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the existing curve to rename, as listed by get_anim_sequence_info (float_curves, transform_curves). |
| `new_curve_name` | string | yes | Name the curve gets after the rename. |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, old_curve_name, new_curve_name, renamed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `rename_bone`

*Destructive.*

Rename a bone in the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset and save it. Fails with an error when old_name is not a bone or new_name is already taken; skeletal meshes and animations that use the old name are not updated. A failed save returns success false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current bone name; must exist in the reference skeleton. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Desired new bone name (must not already exist) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, old_name, new_name, renamed: true, not_found: false, already_used: false, bone_count, saved, save_error?, op: "rename_bone" }`

## `rename_ik_retarget_chain`

*Destructive.*

Rename a retarget chain of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction) and save it. The engine makes the new name unique, so read new_name back; an unknown chain_name is not an error but returns renamed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset path, e.g. "/Game/Retarget/IK_Hero". |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Current name of the retarget chain, as get_ik_rig_info lists it. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Requested new name; the engine may add a suffix to keep it unique. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `rename_montage_section`

*Destructive.*

Rename an existing FCompositeSection on a UAnimMontage by zero-based section_index, in an undo transaction, and save it. The name the section already has (FName match, case ignored) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_index` | number | yes | Zero-based index into CompositeSections (use get_montage_info first to list). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New FName for the section. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_index, old_name, new_name, section_count, sections, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `rename_pose_in_pose_asset`

*Destructive.*

Rename an existing named pose in a UPoseAsset (UPoseAsset::ModifyPoseName) in an undo transaction and save it; renamed is measured by reading the pose names back. An unknown old_pose_name, a new_pose_name another pose already has, or a rename the engine does not take is an error with nothing saved; the same name for both is a success with renamed=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset. |
| `old_pose_name` | string | yes | Current name of the pose to rename. |
| `new_pose_name` | string | yes | New name for the pose. |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, old_pose_name, new_pose_name, renamed, contains_new, contains_old, num_poses, pose_names, saved, save_error, message }`

## `rename_rig_element`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename an element in a Control Rig's hierarchy.  Idempotent: renaming to the current name is a no-op ({ renamed:false, already_named:true }). The engine disambiguates name collisions with a numeric suffix rather than failing, reported honestly via name_adjusted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset |
| `element_type` | string | yes | Element type ("Bone"/"Null"/"Control"/"Curve"/"Socket"/"Connector") |
| `element_name` | string | yes | Current name of the element to rename |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Desired new name for the element |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, old_name: string, element_key: string, element_type: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, name_adjusted: bool, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `rename_skeletal_mesh_morph_target`

*Destructive.*

Rename a morph target on a skeletal mesh asset and save the mesh. Fails if old_name is not a morph target of the mesh or new_name already exists; a failed save also returns an error although the rename stays in memory. Returns old_name, new_name and renamed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero". |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current morph target name, as get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets lists it. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New morph target name; must not already exist on the mesh. |

**Returns:** `{ old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool }`

## `rename_skeletal_mesh_socket`

*Destructive.*

Rename a socket on a skeletal mesh (and its skeleton twin).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current name of the socket |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New name for the socket |

**Returns:** `{ old_name: string, new_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, renamed: bool, already_renamed: bool, socket_count: int }`

## `scaffold_locomotion_animbp`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create or update a character Animation Blueprint with a "Locomotion" state machine + Idle/Walk/Run states + bidirectional transitions between them. Idempotent: re-running on an existing AnimBP returns the existing scaffold.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. "/Game/MyGame". |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name, e.g. "ABP_PlayerLocomotion". |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the target USkeleton. |
| `machine_name` | string | no | Optional state machine name (default "Locomotion"). |
| `states` | array | no | Optional list of state names to add (default ["Idle", "Walk", "Run"]). |
| `add_transitions` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Add Idle&lt;->Walk and Walk&lt;->Run transitions. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, package_path, skeleton_path, machine_name, state_count, transition_count, already_existed, saved }`

## `scale_anim_curve`

*Destructive.*

Retime a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package: every key TIME becomes (t - origin) * factor + origin, and the key VALUES are left untouched -- this stretches/compresses a curve in time, it does not scale its amplitude. FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. A retime that moves no key (factor 1, no keys, or every key at the origin) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `factor` | number | no | Scale factor applied to each key TIME (default 1.0). |
| `origin` | number | no | Time origin the key times are scaled about (default 0.0). |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, origin, factor, num_keys, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_additive_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the additive-animation type and base pose on a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `additive_anim_type` | string | no | Additive type: LocalSpaceBase\|RotationOffsetMeshSpace\|None (default LocalSpaceBase) |
| `ref_pose_type` | string | no | Base pose type: RefPose\|AnimScaled\|AnimFrame\|LocalAnimFrame\|None (default RefPose) |
| `ref_frame_index` | number | no | Frame index used for the base pose (default 0) |
| `ref_pose_anim_path` | string | no | Object path of the reference UAnimSequence for the base pose (optional) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, additive_anim_type, ref_pose_type, ref_frame_index, ref_pose_anim_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }`

## `set_anim_bone_track_keys`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the keys of one bone track of a UAnimSequence with the given per-key transforms (translation, rotation, scale), or, without keys, with num_keys identity keys (zero translation, identity rotation, unit scale), adding the track when it is missing, through its data controller as one undo step, then save the package; num_keys_readback and first_key are read back from the data model. A track that already holds exactly these keys (the stored track data comes out unchanged, measured with the data model GUID; the engine stores a constant track as one value, whatever num_keys is) is a success with changed=false and saved=false, the package keeps the dirty state it had and nothing is saved. A bone_name the sequence's skeleton does not have is an error and nothing is written; an omitted bone_name targets the root bone. keys and num_keys together, an empty keys array or a num_keys below 1 are refused. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Name of a bone of the skeleton of the sequence; omitted or empty means the root bone. |
| `keys` | array | no | Optional array of per-key transforms: { translation:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll] (deg), scale:[x,y,z] }. translation default [0,0,0], rotation default [0,0,0], scale default [1,1,1]. Omitted: num_keys identity keys are written. |
| `num_keys` | number | no | Optional number of identity keys to write when keys is omitted, rounded, >= 1 (default 2); not checked against the frame count of the sequence. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, bone_name, num_keys, num_keys_readback, num_bone_tracks, first_key:{translation,rotation_euler}, identity_keys, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_color`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the editor display color of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (cosmetic: it tints the curve in the editor, it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written; so is a color that is not 3 or 4 numbers. The color the curve already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Create the curve with add_anim_float_curve; its comment: set_anim_curve_comment.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `color` | array | no | Color as [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], usually 0..1 (numbers within the float range); a is 1 when omitted, and an omitted color is white [1,1,1,1]. Any other value is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, color, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_comment`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the author comment of a FLOAT curve on a UAnimSequence through its data controller (one undo step), then save the package (metadata only; it does not affect evaluation). FLOAT-CURVE ONLY: a name that is not a float curve of the sequence, a transform curve included, is an error and nothing is written. The comment the curve already has (case-sensitive) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the float curve. |
| `comment` | string | no | Comment string to set (default empty). |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, comment, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_curve_flags`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the curve flags (the EAnimAssetCurveFlags bitmask) of an existing float or transform curve on a UAnimSequence with one flag, in an undo transaction, then save the package. Despite the name it changes no key interpolation or tangents: linear and editable both set Editable; metadata, drive_track and disabled set those flags. interp_mode is required; an unknown mode, curve or sequence is an error, and any curve_type other than transform means float. old_flags and new_flags are the bitmasks before and after; flags the curve already has are a success with applied=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_curve_data reads the flags.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the curve |
| `interp_mode` | string | yes | One of "linear\|editable\|metadata\|drive_track\|disabled" |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Curve type to target: float (default) or transform |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, interp_mode, old_flags, new_flags, applied, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_frame_rate`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the frame rate of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetFrameRate, one undo step) to fps rounded to whole frames per second, then save the package; fps, numerator and denominator are read back from the data model. The data controller only takes a rate that is a multiple or a factor of the current one, and the frame count must stay whole at the new rate: any other rate is an error and nothing changes. The rate the data model already has is a success with changed=false, saved=false and a note, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_anim_sequence_info reads the rate.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `fps` | number | yes | New frame rate in frames per second, rounded to a whole number that must be at least 1. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path, fps, numerator, denominator, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_graph_node_pin_binding`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind an AnimGraph node input pin to a variable or property path in the node property-binding map (the Details-panel bind chip), e.g. "TransformTrajectory" to "Trajectory"; set_anim_graph_node_property edits the FAnimNode struct instead. Returns applied and the stored binding; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target UAnimGraphNode_* (from get_graph_nodes). |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | The bound property/pin name (e.g. "TransformTrajectory"). |
| `binding_path` | string | yes | The variable/property path to bind the pin to (e.g. "Trajectory", or nested "MyStruct.Member"). This tool does not check that the path resolves. |
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | no | Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint (aliases: anim_blueprint, blueprint_name). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional; deep-resolved; default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `anim_blueprint` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path is absent or empty. |
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path and anim_blueprint are both absent or empty. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pin_name, binding_path, applied, binding:{property_name, property_path[], path_as_text, is_bound, is_promotion, binding_type, pin_category}, saved }`

## `set_anim_graph_node_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one field of an AnimGraphNode's internal FAnimNode struct (runtime settings, not pins): node by NodeGuid, field by name or dotted path. set_properties cannot address a graph node by GUID; this also takes a dotted path, rebuilds the node's pins, is undoable and saves the ABP, but does NOT recompile -- run compile_anim_blueprint. Read: get_anim_graph_node_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target AnimGraphNode. |
| `property` | string | yes | Property path inside the FAnimNode (e.g. "PoseCount", "SlotName"). A leading "Node." is tolerated. Nested structs use dots ("A.B"). |
| `value` | string | no | Text value (UE ImportText form: number, "EnumName", "(X=1,Y=2)"...). Use for scalars/enums/simple structs. |
| `value_json` | any | no | JSON value applied via JsonValueToUProperty. Use for complex/nested types. Takes precedence over value. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, property, applied, new_value, saved }`

## `set_anim_montage_preview_mesh`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the editor preview USkeletalMesh of a UAnimMontage (SetPreviewMesh, one undo step) and save the montage; it only changes what the asset editor shows, and the mesh skeleton is not checked against the montage. Returns mesh_path, prev_mesh_path and applied; the preview mesh the montage already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `mesh_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the preview USkeletalMesh (e.g. '/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, mesh_path, prev_mesh_path, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_montage_skeleton`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rebind a UAnimMontage to a different USkeleton (clears existing source link + recomputes bone caches) in an undo transaction and save it. The skeleton the montage already uses is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the new Skeleton (e.g. '/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, skeleton_path, prev_skeleton_path, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_number_of_frames`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the number of frames of the data model of a UAnimSequence (IAnimationDataController::SetNumberOfFrames, one undo step), then save the package; frame_count is read back from the data model. When the data model rate differs from the sequence sampling rate (as after set_anim_frame_rate), a count that is not a whole number of frames at the sampling rate is an error naming the multiple to use, with nothing changed. Each per-platform override of the sampling rate that the engine compresses at (a valid rate other than the default that is a multiple or a factor of it) is checked the same way, and the error names the platform; an override with a non-positive numerator is an error too. The current count gives saved=false and a note, with nothing saved. A count the data controller rejects is an error with nothing saved, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `frame_count` | number | yes | New number of frames (integer > 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path, frame_count, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_retarget_source`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a UAnimSequence's retarget source (and optionally its retarget reference-pose sequence) in an undo transaction and save it. A ref_pose_seq_path that does not load is an error before anything changes; values the sequence already has are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence to mutate. |
| `retarget_source` | string | no | Retarget-source name (FName). Must name an entry in the owning skeleton's retarget-source map to RESOLVE at runtime, but the property write persists regardless. Use 'None' (or empty) to clear. |
| `ref_pose_seq_path` | string | no | Optional object path of a UAnimSequence used as the additive retarget reference pose (RefPoseSeq). Pass empty/'None' to clear it. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, retarget_source, ref_pose_seq, ref_pose_seq_set, ref_pose_seq_cleared, applied_count, notes, changed, success, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_anim_root_motion`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write the three root motion settings of a UAnimSequence (bEnableRootMotion, RootMotionRootLock, bForceRootLock) and save it. All three are written on every call, so an omitted one is reset to its default; an unknown root lock name applies RefPose while the reply echoes the given text. Settings the sequence already has are a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the sequence is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `enable_root_motion` | boolean | no | Whether to enable root motion extraction (default true) |
| `root_motion_root_lock` | string | no | Root lock mode: RefPose\|AnimFirstFrame\|Zero (default RefPose) |
| `force_root_lock` | boolean | no | Whether to force the root lock (default false) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, enable_root_motion, root_motion_root_lock, force_root_lock, changed, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_anim_transition_rule_automatic`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the automatic rule of one transition (source_state to target_state) in a state machine of an Animation Blueprint: bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState and AutomaticRuleTriggerTime, both written every call (omitted means false and 0). Marks it structurally modified and saves without compiling; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine that owns the transition |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state (transition origin) |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state (transition destination) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | True lets the transition fire on its own when the sequence player of the source state nears its end (bAutomaticRuleBasedOnSequencePlayerInState); omitted writes false. |
| `trigger_time` | number | no | AutomaticRuleTriggerTime in seconds (default 0.0; negative = blend lead) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, enabled, trigger_time, rule_graph_has_result_node, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Make a bool variable the rule of an existing transition (source_state to target_state) of an Animation Blueprint state machine: every rule-graph node but the result sink is removed, then a getter of variable_name is wired to the sink's bCanEnterTransition, so the transition passes while the variable is true (there is no invert option). A missing blueprint, machine, transition or variable, or one that is not a single bool, is an error before anything changes; a variable not compiled yet (variable_kind new_blueprint) is checked against its declared type. Repeat calls rebuild the same rule (idempotent). Marks the blueprint structurally modified and saves without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint). Float test: set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison; time-based: set_anim_transition_rule_automatic; empty rule: clear_anim_transition_rule; new transition: add_anim_transition. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine that owns the transition, matched without case |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state or conduit (transition origin) |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state or conduit (transition destination) |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing bool variable on the AnimBP (or its parent C++ class); the rule reads it as is, true lets the transition pass |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, variable_name, variable_kind, rule_set, sink_present, contributor_count, contributor_node_class, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Make (variable_name operator comparison_value) the rule of an existing transition (source_state to target_state) of an Animation Blueprint state machine: every rule-graph node but the result sink is removed, then a getter, a literal and a comparison node are wired into the sink's bCanEnterTransition. The variable must be a single float of either precision, compiled or only declared (variable_kind new_blueprint), and the test runs in double precision. A missing blueprint, machine, transition or variable, a variable of another type or an unknown operator is an error before anything changes. Repeat calls rebuild the same rule (idempotent); saves without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint). Bool rule: set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool; empty rule: clear_anim_transition_rule. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimBlueprint |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine that owns the transition, matched without case |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state or conduit (transition origin) |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state or conduit (transition destination) |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing float variable (a Blueprint float, or a C++ float or double property) on the AnimBP or its parent class; the left-hand side of the comparison |
| `operator` | string | yes | One of "==", "!=", ">", "&lt;", ">=", "&lt;=" (compared against comparison_value) |
| `comparison_value` | number | no | Right-hand side of the comparison (default 0), written into the double literal node with six decimal places |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, variable_name, operator, comparison_value, variable_kind, rule_set, sink_present, contributor_count, contributor_node_classes, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_animation_speed`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the play rate of a skeletal mesh component, found by object name in the editor world (or the world the world param selects), and switch its component tick on. Only a component in Use Animation Asset (single node) mode takes it: in Animation Blueprint mode nothing changes and actual_speed reads 0, so check speed_set_successfully. Transient: nothing is saved or undoable. A speed outside 0-10 or no such component is an error. For montages use play_animation with play_rate, or set_montage_properties (rate_scale) on the asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `speed` | number | yes | Playback speed multiplier; must be between 0.0 and 10.0 |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, requested_speed: number, previous_speed: number, actual_speed: number, speed_set_successfully: bool, previous_tick_enabled: bool, current_tick_enabled: bool, component_valid: bool, component_class: string, anim_instance_class: string?, has_anim_instance: bool, anim_instance_valid: bool?, warning: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `set_blend_profile_bone`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a bone's blend scale on a UBlendProfile (creates profile if missing).

| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `profile_name` | string | yes | Name of the UBlendProfile (created if absent when create_if_missing=true) |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Bone to scale |
| `scale` | number | yes | Blend scale value (clamped to [0, 1] by UBlendProfile) |
| `create_if_missing` | boolean | no | If true, create the profile when not present (default true) |

## `set_blend_space_interpolation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a blend space's INPUT-SMOOTHING (interpolation) per axis: smoothing time, damping ratio, max speed, smoothing type.  Distinct from set_blend_space_properties (which only sets the BlendParameters axis name/min/max/grid). Writes UBlendSpace::InterpolationParam[axis] via reflection. 1D smooths axis 0 only; 2D smooths X (axis 0) and Y (axis 1). Only the supplied fields change, in one undo transaction, then the blend space is saved; an unknown smoothing type is an error before anything changes, and values the axes already have are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, with nothing modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blend_space_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UBlendSpace / UBlendSpace1D. |
| `x_interpolation_time` | number | no | Optional X-axis smoothing time in seconds (>= 0; 0 disables smoothing). |
| `x_damping_ratio` | number | no | Optional X-axis damping ratio (>= 0; only used when type is SpringDamper). |
| `x_max_speed` | number | no | Optional X-axis maximum speed in real units (>= 0; only used when type is SpringDamper or Exponential). |
| `x_interpolation_type` | string | no | Optional X-axis smoothing type: Averaged\|Linear\|Cubic\|EaseInOut\|Exponential\|SpringDamper. |
| `y_interpolation_time` | number | no | Optional Y-axis smoothing time in seconds (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_damping_ratio` | number | no | Optional Y-axis damping ratio (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_max_speed` | number | no | Optional Y-axis maximum speed (2D only, >= 0). |
| `y_interpolation_type` | string | no | Optional Y-axis smoothing type (2D only): Averaged\|Linear\|Cubic\|EaseInOut\|Exponential\|SpringDamper. |

**Returns:** `{ blend_space_path, is_1d, x_axis: {interpolation_time, damping_ratio, max_speed, interpolation_type}, y_axis: {...}, applied_count, notes, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

## `set_blend_space_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Configure an existing blend space's X and (2D only) Y axis: name, min, max, grid divisions. Over set_properties it addresses each axis field by name, clamps grid to >= 1, rebuilds the runtime sample data (ValidateSampleData/ResampleData) and saves. On a 1D blend space the y_axis_* params are ignored with a note. Only the supplied fields change, in one undo step; min below max is not checked. Values the axes already have are a success with changed=false, applied_count 0, saved=false and a note, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. New blend space: create_blend_space.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blend_space_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UBlendSpace / UBlendSpace1D. |
| `x_axis_name` | string | no | Optional X axis display name. |
| `x_axis_min` | number | no | Optional X axis minimum value. |
| `x_axis_max` | number | no | Optional X axis maximum value. |
| `x_axis_grid` | integer | no | Optional X axis grid divisions (>= 1). |
| `y_axis_name` | string | no | Optional Y axis display name (2D only). |
| `y_axis_min` | number | no | Optional Y axis minimum value (2D only). |
| `y_axis_max` | number | no | Optional Y axis maximum value (2D only). |
| `y_axis_grid` | integer | no | Optional Y axis grid divisions (2D only, >= 1). |

**Returns:** `{ blend_space_path, is_1d, x_axis: {name, min, max, grid}, y_axis: {name, min, max, grid}, applied_count, notes, changed, saved, save_error, note? }`

| `bone_name` | string | yes | Bone to re-parent |
| `parent_name` | string | no | New parent bone name, or empty/null to detach to root |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, parent_name, bone_index, parent_index, updated, not_found, bone_count, saved, op: "set_bone_parent" }`

## `set_bone_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Overwrite the local, parent-relative reference-pose transform of an existing bone in a USkeleton asset loaded by path, through FReferenceSkeletonModifier, then save the skeleton. local_transform is written whole: an omitted location or rotation becomes zero and an omitted or zero scale becomes 1, so to change one component read the others with get_bone_transform first. The modifier notifies the skeleton listeners itself, so commit_bone_changes is not needed. Every call writes and saves, even with the same transform. An unknown bone is an error, so not_found is never true in a reply; a failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the change in memory. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes using it keep their own reference pose. Other bone edits: set_bone_parent, rename_bone, add_bone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USkeleton, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing bone of that skeleton, e.g. "spine_01". |
| `local_transform` | object | yes | Object {location:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll] or {pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:[x,y,z]} relative to the parent bone; the whole transform is written, so an omitted location or rotation becomes zero and an omitted or zero scale becomes 1. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, updated, not_found, bone_count, saved, save_error?, op: "set_bone_transform" }`

## `set_ik_bone_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bone-specific settings for a bone within a solver, as one undo transaction, then save the IK Rig asset; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present in ``settings`` are applied; bone settings are auto-created if absent (a bone the rig skeleton lacks is an error, with nothing changed), and existing settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. FullBodyIK snake_case keys: rotation_stiffness (0-1), position_stiffness (0-1), limit_x/limit_y/limit_z ("Free"/"Limited"/"Locked"), min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y, min_z, max_z, use_preferred_angles (bool), preferred_x, preferred_y, preferred_z. StretchLimb uses its live bone struct's camelCase keys (squashDirection: {x,y,z}). Only FullBodyIK and StretchLimb support per-bone settings; others return an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to modify. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with bone-specific fields to set. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, bone_name: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_goal_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set goal-specific settings for a goal connected to a solver, as one undo transaction, then save the IK Rig asset.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present in ``settings`` are applied. FullBodyIK uses snake_case keys: bone_name, chain_depth (0+), strength_alpha (0-1), pull_chain_alpha (0-1), pin_rotation (0-1). BodyMover uses its live goal struct's camelCase keys (influenceMultiplier 0-10, clamped server-side). Connect the goal first with connect_ik_goal_to_solver. Solvers without per-goal settings return an honest error. Settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of the goal to modify. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with goal-specific fields to set. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, goal_name: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_retarget_chain_bones`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change the start bone, end bone and/or IK goal of an existing retarget chain in an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (each change an undo transaction), then save the asset. Pass at least one of the three, else an error. A missing chain, a bone not in the rig skeleton or a goal_name the rig has no goal for is not an error but start_bone_set, end_bone_set or goal_set false, and that field is left unchanged. A value the chain already has is left alone; when nothing changes, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Siblings: add_ik_retarget_chain, rename_ik_retarget_chain.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Name of the retarget chain to mutate |
| `start_bone` | string | no | Optional new start bone |
| `end_bone` | string | no | Optional new end bone |
| `goal_name` | string | no | Optional new associated IK goal, which must be a goal of the rig; None clears the goal of the chain. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, chain_name: string, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, goal_name: string, start_bone_set: bool, end_bone_set: bool, goal_set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_bones`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the start bone and/or end bone of one solver in an IK Rig asset (0-based stack index) through the IK Rig controller, which records each change as an undo transaction, then save the asset. Pass at least one bone, else an error. An out-of-range index, a bone missing from the rig skeleton, or a start or end bone on a solver type without one is not an error: start_bone_set or end_bone_set comes back false, next to the bones read back, and nothing is stored for it. A bone the solver already has is left alone; when nothing changes, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_ik_solver_details reads them back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |
| `start_bone` | string | no | Optional start bone name |
| `end_bone` | string | no | Optional end bone name |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, start_bone_set: bool, end_bone_set: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_enabled`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Enable or disable the solver at a 0-based index of an IK Rig asset through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset; enabled is read back. An out-of-range index is not an error but set_ok false, and a solver already in the requested state gives changed false: in both cases saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | 0-based solver index |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool; defaults to true |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, enabled: bool, set_ok: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_ik_solver_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set detailed solver-specific settings on a solver in an IK Rig, as one undo transaction, then save the asset.  Partial update: only fields present in ``settings`` are applied (idempotent). FullBodyIK uses snake_case keys: root_bone, iterations (0-1000), sub_iterations (0-1000), mass_multiplier (0-10), allow_stretch (bool), root_behavior (enum string), global_pull_chain_alpha (0-1), max_angle (0-45), over_relaxation (1-2). Other solver types (Limb/Pole/BodyMover/SetTransform/StretchLimb) accept the camelCase names of their live settings struct; ClampMin/ClampMax bounds are enforced server-side. Settings that already have those values give changed false, saved false and a note, with nothing saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |
| `settings` | object | yes | Object with solver-type-specific fields to set. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, solver_index: int, solver_type: string, success: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_montage_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set only the supplied blend-in/blend-out times, global rate scale, blend modes, auto blend out, trigger time, sync group/slot and deprecated root motion fields of a UAnimMontage in one undo step and save it. Over set_properties it sets the blend times through FAlphaBlend::SetBlendTime (clamped to >= 0), validates enum names before any write and saves in the same call; other montage properties: set_properties. Bad enum names, or no field, are refused before any change; values the montage already has give changed=false, applied_count 0 and saved=false, nothing modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `name` | string | no | Alias of montage_path. |
| `blend_in` | number | no | Blend-in time in seconds (BlendIn), clamped to >= 0. Optional. |
| `blend_out` | number | no | Blend-out time in seconds (BlendOut), clamped to >= 0. Optional. |
| `rate_scale` | number | no | Global play rate scale of the montage (RateScale). Optional. |
| `blend_mode_in` | string | no | BlendModeIn: 'Standard' or 'Inertialization' (EMontageBlendMode). Optional. |
| `blend_mode_out` | string | no | BlendModeOut: 'Standard' or 'Inertialization' (EMontageBlendMode). Optional. |
| `enable_auto_blend_out` | boolean | no | When true the montage blends out by itself near its end (bEnableAutoBlendOut); omitted keeps the current value. |
| `blend_out_trigger_time` | number | no | BlendOutTriggerTime in seconds (&lt;0 = auto from BlendOut time). Optional. |
| `sync_group` | string | no | Sync group name (SyncGroup) the montage joins for marker-based sync; an empty string sets None, omitted keeps the current value. |
| `sync_slot_index` | number | no | Zero-based index of the slot track whose animation drives the sync group (SyncSlotIndex); omitted keeps the current value. |
| `enable_root_motion_translation` | boolean | no | bEnableRootMotionTranslation (bool, DEPRECATED since 4.5). Optional. |
| `enable_root_motion_rotation` | boolean | no | bEnableRootMotionRotation (bool, DEPRECATED since 4.5). Optional. |
| `root_motion_root_lock` | string | no | RootMotionRootLock: 'RefPose'\|'AnimFirstFrame'\|'Zero' (DEPRECATED since 4.5). Optional. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, blend_in, blend_out, rate_scale, blend_mode_in, blend_mode_out, enable_auto_blend_out, blend_out_trigger_time, sync_group, sync_slot_index, root_motion: {...}, applied_count, notes, changed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_morph_target_generated_by_engine`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Flag morph targets of a skeletal mesh asset as generated by engine tools rather than imported from a source file, on every LOD, then save the mesh (a failed save is an error). The flag is only ever set, never cleared; names not on the mesh are ignored, and an empty or missing list flags every morph. When any flag changes the engine runs PreEditChange/PostEditChange on the mesh, which rebuilds it. modified says whether anything changed; flagged lists every morph now marked on LOD 0. Names come from get_skeletal_mesh_morph_targets.

| `morph_target_names` | array | no | List of morph target names to flag; empty list = flag every morph on the mesh |
