## `set_motion_warping_component_search_in_anims`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages on the UMotionWarpingComponent of an editor-world actor found by internal name (not label): when true, warping windows are also searched in animations inside montages. Marks the level dirty, not saved; returns previous and new values and changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Sets bSearchForWindowsInAnimsWithinMontages: when true, motion-warping windows are also searched in animations nested inside montages (required, no default) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, previous_search_in_anims: bool, new_search_in_anims: bool, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_bone_name`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the BoneName on an existing FMotionWarpingTarget (resolves the existing Component ref).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Skeletal bone on the target's Component to anchor to; NAME_None follows the component root |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_bone_name: string, new_bone_name: string, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_follow_component`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bFollowComponent on an existing component-based warp target of an editor-world actor found by internal name, keeping its Component, BoneName and offsets. A missing target, or one without a Component, is an error. WarpTargets is Transient, so the change is not saved with the level.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal object name of the actor with the UMotionWarpingComponent, e.g. "BP_Hero_C_0"; the outliner label does not match. |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `follow` | boolean | yes | When true the target tracks the Component's live transform each frame; when false it snapshots the current transform (required, no default) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_follow: bool, new_follow: bool, changed: bool }`

## `set_motion_warping_target_location_offset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set LocationOffset (FVector) on an existing FMotionWarpingTarget (keeps BoneName/follow/rotation-offset).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Engine name of the actor carrying the UMotionWarpingComponent |
| `warp_target_name` | string | yes | FName of the existing warp target on the component |
| `location_offset` | array | no | [x, y, z] offset applied to the target relative to its LocationOffsetDirection |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name, warp_target_name, previous_x, previous_y, previous_z, new_x, new_y, new_z, changed: bool }`

## `set_pose_asset_base_pose`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set which named pose of a UPoseAsset is its base pose (UPoseAsset::SetBasePoseName) in an undo transaction, then save the asset; an empty or None base_pose_name goes back to the skeleton reference pose. A name the asset does not contain is an error before anything changes, and so is a base pose the engine does not take (read back from the asset), with nothing saved. The base pose the asset already has is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. The base pose only drives evaluation of an additive pose asset, which additive and note report. Edit poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset, rename_pose_in_pose_asset and remove_pose_from_pose_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset. |
| `base_pose_name` | string | no | Name of the pose to use as the base; empty/None resets to the reference pose. |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, base_pose_name, requested_name, applied, base_pose_index, is_reference_pose, additive, note, saved, save_error, message }`

## `set_pose_search_database_schema`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind a UPoseSearchSchema to a UPoseSearchDatabase (assigns the Schema field). Use it right after creating a database with no schema, or to rebind an existing one; a database without a schema cannot be indexed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required). |
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to bind (required). |

**Returns:** `{ database_path, previous_schema_path, new_schema_path, changed: bool, saved: bool }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_mirror_data_table`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind (or rebind) the UMirrorDataTable of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role` (default role when omitted). Refused when no entry has that role.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `mirror_data_table_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMirrorDataTable to bind under the given role (required). |
| `role` | string | no | Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, role, previous_mirror_data_table_path, new_mirror_data_table_path, changed, saved }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write scalar UPROPERTYs of a PoseSearchSchema asset (SampleRate, permutations, padding, DataPreprocessor...), clamp them to ClampMin/ClampMax, re-finalize the schema and save; set_properties neither clamps nor saves. changed says whether any written value differs from what the schema held. Keys match property names case-insensitively; an empty object, a key that names no property (the error lists them), Channels or another instanced or deprecated property, a null value, or a value of the wrong kind or that does not convert is an error and nothing changes. Skeleton, mirror table, role: set_pose_search_schema_* tools.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the target UPoseSearchSchema (required). |
| `properties` | object | yes | Object of UPoseSearchSchema UPROPERTY fields to merge; keys are the C++ property NAMES (case-insensitive), absent keys untouched. Covers: SampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), bAddDataPadding(bool), bInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), bDrawInjectAdditionalDebugChannels(bool), NumberOfPermutations(int, ClampMin=1), PermutationsSampleRate(int, ClampMin=1 ClampMax=240), PermutationsTimeOffset(float), DataPreprocessor(enum name: None/Normalize/NormalizeOnlyByDeviation/NormalizeWithCommonSchema). Object-refs (skeleton, mirror_data_table) and the role tag are set via their dedicated commands, not here. An empty object, a key that names no property (or a deprecated one, or one holding instanced subobjects such as Channels), a null value or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is changed. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, asset_class, settings, applied_keys, changed, saved, save_error? }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_role`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename the role (FName) of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under role_from (default role when omitted). Refused when new_role is already taken by another entry.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `new_role` | string | yes | New role name (FName) to assign to the entry, identifying it within a multi-character schema (required). |
| `role_from` | string | no | Existing role name (FName) of the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry to rename (optional; empty = default role). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, previous_role, new_role, changed, saved }`

## `set_pose_search_schema_skeleton`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind (or rebind) the USkeleton, and optionally the UMirrorDataTable, of the schema's FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry under `role`; with a new role it appends a second character's entry to a multi-character schema. Idempotent by role: if an entry already exists under that role its skeleton is REPLACED (and its mirror table when mirror_data_table_path is given), already_existed true; otherwise one entry is appended for that role, added true. Other roles are never touched, and no duplicate role entry is ever pushed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema to edit (required). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the USkeleton to bind under the given role (required). |
| `role` | string | no | Role name (FName) identifying the FPoseSearchRoledSkeleton entry within a multi-character schema (optional; empty = default role). |
| `mirror_data_table_path` | string | no | Optional. Asset path of a UMirrorDataTable to bind under the role: given to the new entry, or written on the existing one. Omitted or empty: a new entry gets none and an existing entry keeps its table. A path that does not load as a UMirrorDataTable is an error and nothing is written. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, role, previous_skeleton_path, new_skeleton_path, previous_mirror_data_table_path, mirror_data_table_path, roled_skeleton_count, added, already_existed, changed, saved }`

## `set_retarget_pose_bone_rotation`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a bone's rotation offset in the current retarget pose (euler degrees) of an IK Retargeter asset, as one undo transaction, then save the asset; the offset is read back as quat_x..quat_w. Creates a default pose if none is current. bone_name is stored as given, not checked against the skeleton. When the pose to edit is already current and already holds exactly that offset for the bone, changed is false, saved is false, a note says so and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to update |
| `source_or_target` | string | no | Optional "Source" or "Target" scope; defaults to "Target" |
| `pitch` | number | no | Euler pitch in degrees (used when no quat is provided) |
| `yaw` | number | no | Euler yaw in degrees |
| `roll` | number | no | Euler roll in degrees |
| `quat_x` | number | no | Optional quaternion X |
| `quat_y` | number | no | Optional quaternion Y |
| `quat_z` | number | no | Optional quaternion Z |
| `quat_w` | number | no | Optional quaternion W |
| `rotation` | object | no | Optional nested {x, y, z, w} quaternion object |
| `pose_name` | string | no | Optional explicit retarget pose name; created if missing |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, bone_name: string, source_or_target: string, retarget_pose: string, quat_x: number, quat_y: number, quat_z: number, quat_w: number, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_retargeter_chain_mapping`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Make source_chain drive target_chain in an IK Retargeter asset, overwriting the previous mapping, on every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain (or only the op named op_name), in one undo transaction, then save the asset. source_chain is not validated, so a misspelled name is stored as given. set_ok is false when no op lists target_chain; mapped_source is read back from the first matching op. When no op lists target_chain, or every one already maps it to source_chain, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. get_ik_retargeter_info shows the per-op mappings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `source_chain` | string | yes | Name of the source retarget chain |
| `target_chain` | string | yes | Name of the target retarget chain to map to |
| `op_name` | string | no | Optional op name as get_ik_retargeter_info lists it; omitted, every op whose chain mapping lists target_chain is updated |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_chain: string, target_chain: string, mapped_source: string, set_ok: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_retargeter_op_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Partial-merge a retarget op's live settings struct (only the JSON fields present are written -> idempotent), and optionally toggle the op enabled flag, as one undo transaction, then save the asset.  Settings keys match get_retargeter_op_info (first char lower-cased, e.g. lODThreshold). Numeric ClampMin/ClampMax metadata is enforced after the merge. The optional `enabled` flag is applied via the controller. The payload echoes the read-back settings. When neither is given, or the op already has those settings and that enabled state, changed is false, saved is false, a note says why and nothing is saved. An out-of-range op_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UIKRetargeter asset. |
| `op_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the op in the retargeter's op stack. |
| `settings` | object | no | Partial settings object; only present fields are written (e.g. { lODThreshold: 5 }). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional: enable/disable the op (applied via the controller). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, enabled: bool, settings: object, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_limits`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a scalar Control Rig control's min/max limits (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer).  Enables the limit array for the control type and sets MinimumValue/MaximumValue type-correctly; once enabled, set_rig_control_value clamps via ApplyLimits. Verified read-back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer). |
| `min` | number | yes | Minimum value (number). |
| `max` | number | yes | Maximum value (number). |
| `enable` | boolean | no | Whether to enable the limits (optional, default true). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, min: number, max: number, limit_enabled: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Edit an existing Control Rig control's shape/gizmo/color/limit-draw settings (the bits add_rig_element can't set when it adds a control).  Read-modify-write: reads the control's FRigControlSettings, applies the provided fields, writes back via URigHierarchyController::SetControlSettings, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. Only the supplied fields change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `display_name` | string | no | Optional display name (FName) for the control. |
| `shape_name` | string | no | Optional gizmo shape name (e.g. "Default", "Box", "Sphere", "Circle"). |
| `shape_color` | array | no | Optional shape color [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A] floats (0..1). |
| `shape_visible` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether the gizmo shape is visible in 3D. |
| `draw_limits` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether to draw the control's limits in debug. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, settings_applied: { display_name, shape_name, shape_color: [float], shape_visible, draw_limits }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_shape_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the local shape (gizmo) transform of an existing Control Rig control.  Reads the current local shape transform, overrides only the supplied location/rotation/scale, writes back via URigHierarchy::SetControlShapeTransform, recompiles + saves, and returns the verified read-back. This positions the manipulator gizmo relative to the control, independent of the control's value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo location. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] gizmo rotation. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [X, Y, Z] gizmo scale. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, shape_transform: { location: [float], rotation: [float], scale: [float] }, applied_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rig_control_value`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a Control Rig control's pose value (Initial + Current), type-correct per the control's ERigControlType.  add_rig_element only seeds a control with the identity value. SetControlValue applies the control's limits, so a value outside an enabled min/max is clamped (set limits first with set_rig_control_limits). Verified read-back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset. |
| `control_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing control element. |
| `value` | any | yes | The value: bool (Bool), number (Float/ScaleFloat/Integer), or [x,y(,z)] (Vector2D/Position/Scale/Rotator). |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, control_name: string, control_type: string, value: any, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_rigvm_pin_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of a pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::SetPinDefaultValue, no undo entry), then compile and save it. success reflects the save even when the write failed: check set, pin_found and current_value, which is read back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UControlRigBlueprint, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin". |
| `pin_path` | string | yes | Pin path NodeName.PinName, e.g. SetTransform.bInitial |
| `value` | string | yes | Value in UE export-text form, e.g. "true", "1.0" or "(X=0.0,Y=0.0,Z=1.0)"; array pins are resized to the given element count. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, pin_path: string, value: string, set: bool, pin_found: bool, current_value: string, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_anim_class`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Repoint a Blueprint's skeletal mesh component AnimClass to a (fork) AnimBlueprint. Also handles the INHERITED native Character Mesh, which is not in the SCS and which the generic component-property setters cannot reach: it writes the CDO component archetype so spawned instances inherit the new AnimClass. Also sets AnimationMode=AnimationBlueprint.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Character/Actor Blueprint (name or path), e.g. "BP_MyCharacter". |
| `anim_class` | string | yes | The AnimBlueprint to use: an ABP asset path (resolved to its generated class) or a "..._C" class path/name. |
| `component_name` | string | no | Skeletal mesh component to target (optional). Omit to target the Character's inherited Mesh. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint, component, anim_class, previous_anim_class, applied, wrote_cdo_archetype, saved }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_component_tick`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Switch the tick of a skeletal mesh component in the editor world (or the one the world param picks): despite the name, it only toggles component ticking and tick-when-paused. Returns the previous and current tick flags; nothing is marked dirty or saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `event_settings` | string | yes | Tick mode, any case: 'enable' (tick on, not while paused), 'disable' (tick off) or 'custom' (tick on, paused setting kept) |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, requested_settings: string, events_configured: bool, previous_tick_enabled: bool, previous_tick_when_paused: bool, current_tick_enabled: bool, current_tick_when_paused: bool, component_valid: bool, component_class: string, anim_instance_class: string?, has_anim_instance: bool, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_build_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change the stored build settings of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset, only the fields you pass, and save the mesh. The mesh is not rebuilt here, so the settings take effect at its next build or reimport; a failed save returns an error. Returns settings_applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Skeletal mesh asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero". |
| `lod_index` | number | no | 0-based LOD index (default 0); an index the mesh does not have fails the call. |
| `recompute_normals` | boolean | no | Ignore the imported normals and recompute them (bRecomputeNormals). |
| `recompute_tangents` | boolean | no | Ignore the imported tangents and recompute them (bRecomputeTangents). |
| `use_mikk_t_space` | boolean | no | Use MikkTSpace when computing tangents (bUseMikkTSpace). |
| `compute_weighted_normals` | boolean | no | Weight computed normals by triangle area and corner angle (bComputeWeightedNormals). |
| `remove_degenerates` | boolean | no | Remove degenerate triangles at build time (bRemoveDegenerates). |
| `high_precision_tangents` | boolean | no | Store tangents at 16-bit instead of 8-bit precision (bUseHighPrecisionTangentBasis). |
| `high_precision_weights` | boolean | no | Use 16-bit instead of 8-bit skin weights for rendering (bUseHighPrecisionSkinWeights). |
| `full_precision_uvs` | boolean | no | Store UVs at full floating-point precision (bUseFullPrecisionUVs). |
| `bone_influence_limit` | number | no | Maximum bone influences per vertex; 0 uses the DefaultBoneInfluenceLimit project setting, and values above the project limit have no effect. |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Author a LOD's FSkeletalMeshOptimizationSettings (ReductionSettings) — the data bake_skeletal_mesh_lod consumes, making the bake steerable instead of running with defaults.  Partial update (idempotent): only fields present are written. Enums are by name (full "SMTC_NumOfTriangles" or short "NumOfTriangles"). termination_criterion (SMTC_*) and reduction_method (SMOT_*) are DISTINCT.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset. |
| `lod_index` | number | no | LOD index to modify (default 0). |
| `termination_criterion` | string | no | SMTC_*: NumOfTriangles\|NumOfVerts\|TriangleOrVert\|AbsNumOfTriangles\|AbsNumOfVerts\|AbsTriangleOrVert. |
| `reduction_method` | string | no | SMOT_*: NumOfTriangles\|MaxDeviation\|TriangleOrDeviation. |
| `num_of_triangles_percentage` | number | no | float ratio of triangles to retain (0.1 = 10%). |
| `num_of_vert_percentage` | number | no | float ratio of vertices to retain. |
| `max_deviation_percentage` | number | no | float [0,1], accuracy target when reduction_method=MaxDeviation. |
| `max_num_of_triangles` | number | no | int absolute triangle cap (ClampMin 4). |
| `max_num_of_verts` | number | no | int absolute vertex cap (ClampMin 6). |
| `max_num_of_triangles_percentage` | number | no | int (editor-only) cap when using percentage criterion (ClampMin 4). |
| `max_num_of_verts_percentage` | number | no | int (editor-only) cap when using percentage criterion (ClampMin 6). |
| `base_lod` | number | no | int base LOD index to generate from (default 0). |
| `silhouette_importance` | string | no | SMOI_*: Off\|Lowest\|Low\|Normal\|High\|Highest. |
| `texture_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of texture density. |
| `shading_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of shading quality. |
| `skinning_importance` | string | no | SMOI_* importance of skinning quality. |
| `max_bones_per_vertex` | number | no | int max bone influences per vertex (ClampMin 1). |
| `welding_threshold` | number | no | float vertex weld distance. |
| `normals_threshold` | number | no | float hard-edge angle in degrees (used when recalc_normals). |
| `recalc_normals` | boolean | no | bool recompute normals. |
| `remap_morph_targets` | boolean | no | bool remap morph targets onto the reduced LOD. |
| `enforce_bone_boundaries` | boolean | no | bool penalize collapses across different major bones. |

**Returns:** `{ lod_index: int, settings_applied: {...}, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the flat per-LOD scalars/enums of FSkeletalMeshLODInfo that no other setter covers (screen size, hysteresis, CPU access, morph error tolerance, skin cache usage, mesh deformer, prioritization weight) on one LOD or, with lod_index -1 or "all", on every LOD of the mesh, then save the mesh. Partial update (idempotent): only fields present are written; a bad skin_cache_usage or lod_index is refused before anything is written. A failed save is an error that leaves the change in memory. Per-platform screen-size overrides are left as they are.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset. |
| `lod_index` | any | no | Optional. 0-based LOD index to modify (default 0), or -1 / "all" for every LOD. allow_cpu_access with every LOD goes through USkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem::SetAllowCPUAccess. |
| `screen_size` | number | no | Optional float, ScreenSize.Default: the screen size at which this LOD switches in (e.g. 0.3). |
| `lod_hysteresis` | number | no | float, avoids flickering at the LOD boundary. |
| `allow_cpu_access` | boolean | no | bool, keep this LOD's data on the CPU (e.g. for FX sampling). |
| `morph_target_position_error_tolerance` | number | no | float in microns, Clamp 0.01..10000 (default 20). |
| `skin_cache_usage` | string | no | ESkinCacheUsage by NAME: Auto\|Disabled\|Enabled (Disabled=255, parsed by name). |
| `allow_mesh_deformer` | boolean | no | bool, whether a Mesh Deformer is used on this LOD. |
| `weight_of_prioritization` | number | no | float >=0, weight given to BonesToPrioritize/SectionsToPrioritize. |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int (-1 for every LOD), all_lods: bool, applied_lods: int, settings_applied: {...}, old_screen_size?: float (one LOD), old_screen_sizes?: [float] (every LOD), saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_material_slot`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Assign a material to an existing material slot of a skeletal mesh ASSET (writes FSkeletalMaterial.MaterialInterface in USkeletalMesh::GetMaterials()). Address the slot by slot_index OR slot_name (exactly one). Never auto-grows the slot array.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the USkeletalMesh asset. |
| `material_path` | string | yes | Content path to the UMaterialInterface to assign. |
| `slot_index` | number | no | Zero-based index of an existing material slot (mutually exclusive with slot_name). |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Name of an existing material slot to resolve to its index (mutually exclusive with slot_index). |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, slot_index: int, slot_name: string, material_path: string, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_min_lod`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the minimum LOD a skeletal mesh asset (found by content path) renders, so the more detailed LODs below it are skipped while they stay in the asset. It replaces the whole Minimum LOD property with this one value, per-platform overrides included, or the per-quality-level one when the project setting UseSkeletalMeshMinLODPerQualityLevels is on. A missing min_lod, one outside 0 to the LOD count minus 1, or a mesh that does not load is an error. One undo step; the mesh is marked dirty but not saved, so follow with save_asset. old_min_lod is the value in effect before the call. To take a LOD out of the asset use remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; to change switch distances, set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings with screen_size.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `min_lod` | number | yes | New minimum LOD index, 0-based (must be in [0, NumLODs-1]) |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_min_lod: int, min_lod: int, lod_count: int, applied: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_section_flags`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn shadow casting, runtime tangent recomputation (a GPU skin cache feature) and/or ray-tracing visibility on or off for one section of one LOD of a skeletal mesh asset found by content path; pass at least one of the three flags, and only the flags passed are written. The SkeletalMeshEditorSubsystem writes the section's user data (one undo step per flag) and rebuilds the render data, then the mesh is saved. A mesh that does not load, a LOD or section index its imported model does not have, or a call during PIE (the subsystem refuses it) is an error, and the flags written before the refused one stay in memory unsaved; so is a failed save, which leaves the change in memory. Setting the current value again re-applies and re-saves it. Read the section flags with get_skeletal_mesh_section_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `lod_index` | number | no | 0-based LOD index containing the section (default 0) |
| `section_index` | number | no | 0-based index of the section within that LOD, as get_skeletal_mesh_section_info lists it (default 0) |
| `cast_shadow` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether the section casts shadows. |
| `recompute_tangent` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether the GPU skin cache recomputes the section's tangents at runtime. |
| `visible_in_ray_tracing` | boolean | no | Optional bool: whether the section is visible in ray tracing (bVisibleInRayTracing). b_visible is accepted as an alias. |
| `b_visible` | boolean | no |   |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, section_index: int, cast_shadow?: bool, recompute_tangent?: bool, visible_in_ray_tracing?: bool, saved: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_socket_parent`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Re-parent an existing socket on a skeletal mesh to a different bone. Validates the bone exists in the reference skeleton.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to re-parent |
| `parent_bone_name` | string | yes | Bone name to attach the socket to (must exist in skeleton) |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, parent_bone_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, reparented: bool }`

## `set_skeletal_mesh_socket_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the local transform (relative to parent bone) of a socket on a skeletal mesh. All three of location/rotation/scale are optional; only fields present are written.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket to modify |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation (degrees) |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative scale |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, skeletal_mesh_path: string, applied: {location, rotation, scale}, location_x: float, location_y: float, location_z: float, rotation_pitch: float, rotation_yaw: float, rotation_roll: float, scale_x: float, scale_y: float, scale_z: float }`

## `setup_foot_ik`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a Leg IK node (UAnimGraphNode_LegIK) to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, or reuse the first one already there, bind the feet into its LegsDefinition, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Leg 0 gets left_foot_bone and leg 1 right_foot_bone as the FK foot bone; a leg's IK target bone is set to the same bone when it is unset or the leg's foot changes, so the node compiles but has no effect until each IK target names an IK bone (set_anim_graph_node_property on LegsDefinition with the returned node_id); legs beyond the first two and the other leg settings are kept. Bones the target skeleton lacks are an error and nothing is written. The node is left unwired: connect it with connect_anim_graph_pins. Idempotent; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset. |
| `left_foot_bone` | string | yes | Left foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 0; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one. |
| `right_foot_bone` | string | yes | Right foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 1; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, node_id, left_foot_bone, right_foot_bone, legs: [{ fk_foot_bone, ik_foot_bone, num_bones_in_limb }], bones_checked_against, ik_node_count, already_existed, saved, save_error }`

## `sort_montage_segments`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Sort the segments of one slot track of a UAnimMontage asset by their position on the track, ascending (FAnimTrack::SortAnimSegments), which then lays them end-to-end from 0 and clamps each segment's end time to its animation's length, in one undo step, and save the montage. Segment indices follow the new order, and the sort key is the track position, not the AnimStartTime that set_montage_segment_start_time edits. Idempotent: a track the sort leaves unchanged (already in order, end-to-end and within its animations) is a success with applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is modified or saved. An unknown montage or slot is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. To close gaps but keep the array order: collapse_montage_segments; slot names: get_montage_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `slot_name` | string | yes | Name of the slot track to sort, e.g. "DefaultSlot" (case-insensitive); an unknown slot is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, slot_name, segment_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `stop_animation`

*Destructive.*

Stop montage playback on a skeletal mesh component with Montage_Stop and a 0.25 s blend-out: only montage_path when given, otherwise every active montage. Editor world unless the world param says otherwise; an unknown montage_path is an error. was_playing and playing cover any montage.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_name` | string | yes | Object name of the USkeletalMeshComponent, e.g. "CharacterMesh0", case-insensitive; the first actor in the world that has one with that name wins |
| `montage_path` | string | no | Full asset path of a specific AnimMontage to stop; if omitted, stops all montages (optional) |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, was_playing: bool, playing: bool, success: bool, montage_path: string?, montage_name: string?, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`
